Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

OSWorld: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents for Open-Ended Tasks in Real Computer Environments (2404.07972v1) · paper method: OSWorld tasks pair instructions with initial-state setup and manually crafted evaluation scripts; the paper reports nine computer-science student authors spending over three months and about 1,800 person-hours on construction and checking.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

OSWorld: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents for Open-Ended Tasks in Real Computer Environments (2404.07972v1) · paper method: The OSWorld human evaluation uses computer-science-major college students with basic software skills who had not previously seen the samples or software; their time and correctness are measured for each example.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

OSWorld: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents for Open-Ended Tasks in Real Computer Environments (2404.07972v1) · paper method: The paper states that its evaluation functions mainly assess task-completion correctness and do not efficiently detect latent unnecessary damaging side effects.
